display_name: US OSHA permissible exposure limits (Table Z-1)
source_citation: United States Code of Federal Regulations, Title 29, Part 1910, Section 1910.1000, Table Z-1. Text as served by eCFR.
known_limitations: THIS IS NOT A SAFETY ASSESSMENT. A permissible exposure limit constrains airborne concentration in an occupational setting; it is not a property of the substance and does not speak to any other exposure route, to the general population, or to whether a given use is safe.

Table Z-1 lists 500 rows and 390 of them state a limit here. 22 give their value as (2) or (3), meaning Table Z-2 or Z-3 of the same section holds it, and 87 name another section or another entry instead. Neither Z-2 nor Z-3 is encoded, so this ruleset is silent about those substances rather than saying they are unlimited.
1 row is listed with no PEL printed at all, and is encoded as no rule rather than as a limit of zero.

Values are carried exactly as printed. No ppm to mg/m3 conversion is performed: it needs the substance's molar mass as well as the stated 25 C and 760 torr, so a converted number would carry an assumption the regulation does not make.
